From b6f6118901d1e867ac9177bbff3b00b185bd4fdc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Feb 2020 11:52:29 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] ipv6: restrict IPV6_ADDRFORM operation

IPV6_ADDRFORM is able to transform IPv6 socket to IPv4 one.
While this operation sounds illogical, we have to support it.

One of the things it does for TCP socket is to switch sk->sk_prot
to tcp_prot.

We now have other layers playing with sk->sk_prot, so we should make
sure to not interfere with them.

This patch makes sure sk_prot is the default pointer for TCP IPv6 socket.

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ipv6_sockglue.c b/net/ipv6/ipv6_sockglue.c
index 79fc012dd2ca..debdaeba5d8c 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/ipv6_sockglue.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/ipv6_sockglue.c
@@ -183,9 +183,15 @@ static int do_ipv6_setsockopt(struct sock *sk, int level, int optname,
 					retv = -EBUSY;
 					break;
 				}
-			} else if (sk->sk_protocol != IPPROTO_TCP)
+			} else if (sk->sk_protocol == IPPROTO_TCP) {
+				if (sk->sk_prot != &tcpv6_prot) {
+					retv = -EBUSY;
+					break;
+				}
 				break;
-
+			} else {
+				break;
+			}
 			if (sk->sk_state != TCP_ESTABLISHED) {
 				retv = -ENOTCONN;
 				break;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/ipv6/ipv6_sockglue.c`**
   - The code block handling the `IPV6_ADDRFORM` operation was modified to ensure that the socket's protocol (`sk->sk_prot`) is checked against `tcpv6_prot` when the socket's protocol (`sk->sk_protocol`) is `IPPROTO_TCP`.
   - If the socket's protocol is not `tcpv6_prot`, the operation will return `-EBUSY`, preventing the transformation of the socket.
   - The structure of the conditional statements was adjusted to improve clarity and ensure that the logic correctly handles the TCP socket case.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes in `ipv6_sockglue.c` are directly related to the handling of the `IPV6_ADDRFORM` operation for TCP sockets. The patch aims to prevent unintended modifications to the socket's protocol when it is already set to `tcpv6_prot`, thereby addressing the reported kernel NULL pointer dereference bug. By ensuring that the socket's protocol is validated before any changes are made, the patch enhances the stability and correctness of the socket operations in the IPv6 context.

        The bug was caused by the `IPV6_ADDRFORM` operation allowing the transformation of an IPv6 socket to an IPv4 socket without proper checks on the socket's protocol. This could lead to a situation where the socket's protocol pointer (`sk->sk_prot`) was not correctly set, resulting in a NULL pointer dereference when the system attempted to access it, leading to a crash.
        
        Commit message:
        ipv6: restrict IPV6_ADDRFORM operation

IPV6_ADDRFORM is able to transform IPv6 socket to IPv4 one.
While this operation sounds illogical, we have to support it.

One of the things it does for TCP socket is to switch sk->sk_prot
to tcp_prot.

We now have other layers playing with sk->sk_prot, so we should make
sure to not interfere with them.

This patch makes sure sk_prot is the default pointer for TCP IPv6 socket.
